newsitem.title: USA: Dayton Hudson votes replacement rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Dayton Hudson votes replacement rights plan.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said Wednesday it adopted a shareholder rights plan that will replace an existing plan which expires September 26.
It said the new plan is substantially similar to the expiring plan except for the new plan's shorter five-year term.
Dayton said the new plan was not adopted in response to any present effort to acquire the company or its securities.

The plan grants Dayton Hudson investors a form of a preferred share purchase right. Under both the expiring plan and the new plan, generally this right becomes exercisable only in the event a third party accumulates 20 percent or more of the company's common shares.
In that event, each right (except for rights held by the 20 percent shareholder) allows its holders to buy $200 of Dayton Hudson common stock for $100.
